A1.justification: Both complete 32-page PDFs describe the same work, Safely Learning Controlled Stochastic Dynamics. Their text, equations, figures, table, and Appendices A–C are readable and reliably matchable.

before.justification: v2 reports original stochastic-system simulations, safety/reset prediction errors in Table 1, runtime measurements, and supplementary prediction and information-gain results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original simulation, prediction-error, runtime, and supplementary experimental results in Section 6 and Appendices B–C.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithms 1–4 retain the same density estimators, kernel regressors, feasibility tests, and sampling/stopping procedures. The appendix corrections concern supporting bounds; their coefficients coincide under the main theorem’s setting λ = 1/N.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic two-dimensional second-order stochastic system, control space, safety/reset regions, and validation/test controls. No additional dataset, domain, or test scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Section 6 retains comparisons among the same four safety/reset threshold configurations. Neither version evaluates external baseline methods; comparisons with safe reinforcement-learning baselines remain future work in Section 7.

E3.justification: The experimental settings remain identical, including 1000 exploration iterations, 1000 prediction evaluations, and 100-sample Monte Carlo ground truth. Metrics, supplementary prediction grids, and test procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: The threshold-dependent safety and exploration analyses, density-prediction case study in Figure 7, and information-gain analysis in Figure 8 are retained without changes.

E5.justification: Appendix A.3 revises the analytical confidence-interval radii for safety, reset, and density estimation, replacing the error multiplier λ^(-1)N^(-1/2) with λ^(-1/2). This changes their stated calibration for general λ; Table 1’s standard-deviation reporting and Appendix B.4’s 20-run timing reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1, all experimental figure graphics, and the reported runtimes are unchanged. For example, both versions report safety MSE 0.7010 ± 0.3847 at ε = ξ = 0.1 and total training time 31.77 ± 0.38 minutes.

T1.justification: Lemmas A.1–A.2 and the proof of Theorem A.8 correct the N/λ scaling of estimation-error bounds. Equation (39) loses an erroneous N^(-1/2) factor, and equations (40) and (50) use λ^(-1/2). This is a localized mathematical correction; the main theorem’s assumptions, rates, and conclusions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims of safe exploration, joint dynamics/safety/reset estimation, Sobolev-adaptive guarantees, and experimental effectiveness.

C2.justification: The interpretations of the safety–exploration tradeoff and prediction results are unchanged. Qualifications concerning prior norm bounds, low-dimensional validation, computational cost, and future physical-system testing are also retained.

D1.justification: Section 6 and Appendix B retain the same implementation descriptions, hyperparameter-tuning guidance, computational complexities, hardware specifications, and code-access information.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 and the bibliography are unchanged. Both versions position the contribution identically relative to safe Bayesian optimization, safe reinforcement learning, and stochastic-dynamics estimation.

P1.justification: The arXiv version/date stamp changes. Otherwise, the prose, terminology, headings, and section organization remain unchanged; the substantive edits are mathematical.

P2.justification: Appendix equations and text reflow, moving the start of Section B.3 from page 31 to page 30 and shifting Figure 8 upward on page 32. No figure or table is added, removed, or redesigned.

improvement.justification: v3 repairs a specific normalization and regularization-scaling error in the confidence-bound derivation and consistently propagates it through the related appendix bounds. This improves mathematical reliability, but the gain is limited: the old and new coefficients agree for λ = 1/N used in Theorem 5.1, and the main claims and experimental evidence are unchanged.
